prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: pinacol rearrangement: pinacol -> pinacolone (acid-catalyzed). Reactant SMILES: [OH3+].CC(C)(O)C(C)(C)O; product SMILES: [OH3+].CC(=O)C(C)(C)C.O; total charge 1, multiplicity 1; conditions: concentrated H2SO4, heated. Within the allowed methods, model the system so that it approximates the real conditions stated above as closely as the level of theory permits. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [OH2+:1]([H:2]).[CH3:3][C:4]([CH3:5])([OH:6])[C:7]([CH3:8])([CH3:9])[O:10][H:11]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. Use exactly this JSON shape (key names matter: nodes carry `id`, `role` (one of reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state) and `smiles` (a list of SMILES strings), and may optionally carry a `properties` object for declared quantities; edges carry `id`, `from`, `to`, `via`, `bond_changes` and optionally `barrier_kcal_mol`, `channel` and `favored`): {"nodes": [{"id": "RC", "role": "reactant", "smiles": ["..."]}, {"id": "TS1", "role": "transition_state", "smiles": []}, {"id": "P", "role": "product", "smiles": ["..."]}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "RC", "to": "P", "via": "TS1", "bond_changes": {"break": [[1, 2]], "form": [[1, 5]]}, "barrier_kcal_mol": 21.3}]}. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. Declare every barrier you actually compute in kcal/mol on that elementary step's edge as `barrier_kcal_mol` in mechanism_graph.json. Barriers are electronic energy differences (ΔE‡) in kcal/mol, without ZPE or thermal corrections, each relative to that step's own starting minimum: for a bimolecular reaction that minimum is the reactant complex (e.g. the ion-dipole complex), and for a unimolecular process it is simply the reactant minimum. The scorer derives every declared step barrier from your log files and takes the highest as the rate-determining step; a barrier that is undeclared, has no bound ORCA/Gaussian log, or disagrees with those logs is not scorable. Every species node and transition-state node must declare `properties.energy_hartree` (the electronic energy of the geometry you delivered for that node, in Hartree, exactly as it appears in that node's evidence log) and `properties.evidence_log` (the sandbox-relative path of that log). The scorer uses the declared energy to identify which evidence file you delivered for each node; a node missing either field violates the delivery contract. A transition-state evidence file must carry `smiles: <the SMILES of that step's reactant>` so the scorer can attach the saddle to the step it belongs to. Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to xTB and B3LYP-D3(BJ)/def2-SVP; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

edges.step_type: proton transfer from H3O+ to one pinacol OH (leaving-group activation)
